chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Beware of two traits, for in these two were destroyed those who were destroyed: beware of issuing fatwas to the people based on your own opinion, or following as religion that which you do not know.

key_terms.إِيَّاكَ: Emphatic warning formula: 'beware of' / 'be on guard against'
key_terms.بِرَأْيِكَ: By your own opinion — personal reasoning without transmitted knowledge
key_terms.تَدِينَ: To make something a religion, to follow as a religious practice
key_terms.تُفْتِيَ: To issue a fatwa (religious ruling/legal opinion)
key_terms.خَصْلَتَيْنِ: Two traits/characteristics — referring to the two forbidden practices

ai.seo_question: What are the two things Imam al-Sadiq warned against in matters of religion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns his companion Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj of two spiritually catastrophic traits: issuing religious rulings (fatwas) based on personal opinion rather than transmitted knowledge, and adopting as religion that which one does not truly know. This teaching addresses a core epistemological concern in Shia jurisprudence — that religious authority must be grounded in verified knowledge from the Imams, not personal reasoning. The audience of companions would have understood this as a direct injunction against the practice of ra'y (opinion-based jurisprudence) that was prevalent among some schools of the time.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubed, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjal who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of two characteristics, for in these two were destroyed, the one who was destroyed. Beware of issuing Fatwas to the people by your opinion, or making a Religion with that which you do not know’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn ’Abd al-Rahman from ’Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following. “

Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘Beware of two forms of behavior. It is such behaviors that have lead many people to their destruction. Beware of giving fatwa to people on the basis of your own opinion and to follow a religion without knowledge.’”
